accepted.s: Since the 2020 notification, the classification of an MSME is based on which of the following?
o: Investment in land and number of employees
Investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover
accepted.x: The post-2020 classification uses a composite criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment together with annual turnover. The earlier distinction between manufacturing and services was removed.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official basis instead of a related but incorrect indicator.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of MSME classification:
1. In 1950, a small-scale industrial unit had an investment ceiling of ₹5 lakh.
2. The Industrial Policy of 1991 raised the investment ceiling for SSI units.
3. The 2006 framework prescribed separate limits for manufacturing and services.
4. The composite investment-and-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The major milestones were the ₹5 lakh ceiling in 1950, the 1991 increase, separate 2006 limits, and the composite criterion notified on 1 June 2020.
accepted.tq: Check each dated milestone separately before selecting the comprehensive code.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s: Under the 2020 notification, an enterprise with investment of ₹8 crore and annual turnover of ₹40 crore falls under which category?
accepted.x: Under the 2020 limits, a small enterprise could have investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore. The given enterprise falls within both limits.
accepted.tq: Apply both limbs of the composite criterion rather than using investment alone.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2020 MSME limits for a medium enterprise?
o: Investment up to ₹25 crore and turnover up to ₹100 crore
Investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore
Investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore
Investment up to ₹125 crore and turnover up to ₹500 crore
accepted.x: The 2020 notification prescribed an investment limit of ₹50 crore and a turnover limit of ₹250 crore for a medium enterprise.
accepted.tq: Match the category with both numerical thresholds, not just one figure.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s:
With reference to the revised limits applicable from 1 April 2025, consider the following pairs:
1. Micro — ₹2.5 crore investment and ₹10 crore turnover
2. Small — ₹25 crore investment and ₹100 crore turnover
3. Medium — ₹125 crore investment and ₹500 crore turnover
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs correctly state the revised limits from 1 April 2025: ₹2.5/10 crore for micro, ₹25/100 crore for small, and ₹125/500 crore for medium enterprises.
accepted.tq: Read the investment and turnover columns together and distinguish the revised figures from the earlier 2020 limits.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 2020 limits from the limits revised from 1 April 2025?
o: Only the turnover limits were revised in 2025, while investment limits remained unchanged.
The 2020 medium limit was ₹50 crore investment and ₹250 crore turnover; the revised limit is ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore.
The 2020 medium limit was ₹125 crore investment and ₹500 crore turnover; the revised limit is ₹50 crore and ₹250 crore.
Only the micro limits were revised in 2025.
accepted.x: The 2020 medium-enterprise limits were ₹50 crore investment and ₹250 crore turnover. From 1 April 2025, these became ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore respectively.
accepted.tq: Separate the earlier and later figures before comparing the two policy regimes.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh, a mega project is defined as one providing at least how many direct jobs?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh defines mega projects as projects providing 2,000 or more direct jobs.
accepted.tq: Test the state-specific numerical threshold independently of the central MSME classification.
accepted.sec: MSME definition - basis of classification, revision history, micro/small/medium thresholds

accepted.s: The Small and Medium Enterprise Development Bill, introduced on 12 May 2005, subsequently became which legislation?
accepted.x: The Bill introduced on 12 May 2005 became the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006.
accepted.tq: Use the legislative transition from the Bill to the enacted law.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: The MSMED Act, 2006 came into force on:
accepted.x: The MSMED Act, 2006 came into force on 2 October 2006. Its Bill had been introduced on 12 May 2005.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of introduction of the Bill from the date on which the Act came into force.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: Under the original 2006 classification, a manufacturing enterprise with investment of up to ₹25 lakh in plant and machinery was classified as a:
accepted.x: The original 2006 manufacturing ceiling for a micro enterprise was investment up to ₹25 lakh in plant and machinery.
accepted.tq: Recall the category-specific manufacturing ceiling from the original framework.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched under the original 2006 MSMED definitions?
o: Small services — equipment up to ₹5 crore
Small manufacturing — plant and machinery up to ₹5 crore
Micro manufacturing — equipment up to ₹10 lakh
Medium manufacturing — plant and machinery up to ₹5 crore
accepted.x: The original 2006 limit for a small manufacturing enterprise was investment up to ₹5 crore in plant and machinery. The corresponding service limit was ₹2 crore.
accepted.tq: Watch for swaps between manufacturing and services and between adjacent enterprise categories.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s:
With reference to the original 2006 service-sector limits, consider the following statements:
1. A micro service enterprise could have equipment investment up to ₹10 lakh.
2. A small service enterprise could have equipment investment up to ₹2 crore.
3. A medium service enterprise could have equipment investment up to ₹5 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The original service-sector limits were ₹10 lakh for micro, ₹2 crore for small, and ₹5 crore for medium enterprises.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete service-sector column instead of transferring manufacturing limits.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the delayed-payment provision under Chapter V of the MSMED Act?
o: The buyer must pay within 45 days, after which compound interest is charged at three times the RBI bank rate.
The buyer must pay within 30 days, after which compound interest is charged at twice the RBI bank rate.
The buyer must pay within 15 days, after which simple interest is charged at the RBI bank rate.
The buyer must pay within 60 days, after which no statutory interest is payable.
accepted.x: Chapter V requires payment within 45 days. Beyond that period, compound interest is payable at three times the RBI bank rate.
accepted.tq: Combine the payment period with the exact interest multiplier; both parts must be correct.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: Disputes relating to delayed payments to micro and small enterprises are referred to which body?
accepted.x: Disputes concerning delayed payments are referred to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council.
accepted.tq: Identify the specialised statutory forum rather than a general commercial or financial institution.
accepted.sec: MSMED Act 2006 - year passed, original definitions for manufacturing and services

accepted.s: SIDBI was established on 2 April 1990 under which legislation?
accepted.x: SIDBI was set up on 2 April 1990 under the SIDBI Act, 1989.
accepted.tq: Link the institution, establishment date and parent legislation precisely.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the primary role of SIDBI?
o: Apex institution for MSME finance, promotion and development
Authority for administering the Public Distribution System
accepted.x: SIDBI is the apex institution for finance, promotion and development of micro, small and medium enterprises.
accepted.tq: Choose the institutional mandate rather than a function belonging to another economic authority.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: The headquarters of SIDBI is located at:
accepted.x: SIDBI has its headquarters at Lucknow.
accepted.tq: Use location as the distinguishing fact among major financial institutions.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: SIDBI co-founded the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) in:
accepted.x: CGTMSE was co-founded by the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI in 2000 to provide credit guarantee support for collateral-free lending.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of SIDBI’s establishment from the later year of CGTMSE’s formation.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: The corpus contribution ratio between the Government and SIDBI in CGTMSE is:
accepted.x: The corpus of CGTMSE is shared between the Government and SIDBI in the ratio of 4:1.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact institutional contribution ratio rather than the scheme’s broad objective.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding SIDBI is NOT correct?
o: It is an apex institution for MSME finance and development.
It partnered with SVC Co-operative Bank for MSME lending in July 2022.
accepted.x: SIDBI is headquartered in Lucknow, not Hyderabad. The other statements correctly describe its establishment, role and 2022 partnership.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect location while retaining the institution’s other correctly stated attributes.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: State Financial Corporations primarily function as:
o: Agencies administering customs duties on imports
Institutions issuing currency on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India
Central regulators of stock exchanges under the SEBI Act
State-level term lenders to small industries under the SFC Act, 1951
accepted.x: State Financial Corporations provide state-level term lending to small industries under the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Match the financial institution with its level of operation and lending function.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to SIDBI’s MSME-related initiatives?
o: PM SVANidhi — SIDBI is the implementing agency
CGTMSE — established exclusively by the World Bank
TReDS — offline cash payment of MSME invoices
accepted.x: SIDBI is the implementing agency for PM SVANidhi. CGTMSE was co-founded by the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI, the SVC partnership occurred in July 2022, and TReDS is an online invoice-discounting system.
accepted.tq: Separate SIDBI’s implementation, partnership and guarantee roles from incorrect institutional or functional swaps.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: TReDS is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: TReDS is an online platform mechanism for discounting MSME invoices and improving their working-capital access.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact financial function represented by the digital platform.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a TReDS platform mentioned in connection with MSME invoice discounting?
accepted.x: RXIL, A.TReDS (Invoicemart) and M1xchange are TReDS platforms. CGTMSE is a credit-guarantee trust, not a TReDS platform.
accepted.tq: Distinguish platforms for invoice discounting from the separate credit-guarantee institution.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s: Which of the following measures is associated with the Budget 2026-27 provisions relating to MSME receivables?
o: All CPSE purchases from MSMEs are to be settled on TReDS.
MSME invoices are prohibited from being discounted on digital platforms.
GeM is to be delinked from TReDS.
Receivables are excluded from asset-backed securities.
accepted.x: The Budget 2026-27 measures include settlement of all CPSE purchases from MSMEs on TReDS, CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting, a GeM-TReDS link and treatment of receivables as asset-backed securities.
accepted.tq: Select the positive policy measure while rejecting reversed or exclusionary formulations.
accepted.sec: SIDBI - year established, role, partnerships for MSME finance

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to SSI reservation in chronological order:
A. Reservation began with 47 items
B. Reservation reached about 873 items
C. The Abid Hussain Committee submitted its recommendations
D. The last 20 reserved items were dereserved
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Reservation began in 1967, peaked at about 873 items in 1984, the Abid Hussain Committee made its recommendations in 1997, and the last 20 items were dereserved in 2015.
accepted.tq: Fix the dated first and last events, then place the intermediate milestones.
accepted.sec: SSI reservation - number of reserved items over time, dereservation committee

accepted.s: SSI reservation in India began in 1967 with how many items?
accepted.x: Reservation for the small-scale sector began in 1967 with 47 items.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the initial number from the later peak and the final number of items dereserved.
accepted.sec: SSI reservation - number of reserved items over time, dereservation committee

accepted.s: The number of items reserved for the SSI sector reached its approximate peak in 1984 at:
accepted.x: The number of reserved items peaked at approximately 873 in 1984.
accepted.tq: Use the date and peak value together rather than confusing it with the starting figure.
accepted.sec: SSI reservation - number of reserved items over time, dereservation committee

accepted.s: The last 20 items under SSI reservation were dereserved in:
accepted.x: The last 20 items were dereserved in 2015, completing the phasing out of SSI reservation.
accepted.tq: Recall the terminal event in a policy phase-out sequence.
accepted.sec: SSI reservation - number of reserved items over time, dereservation committee
